method.help: Which WhatsApp connection surface to use. Cloud = official Meta Cloud API. Gateway = your own Baileys/wa-gateway server. Bot = WhatsApp Business API platform (360dialog/Twilio-style). SaaS = a third-party messaging provider.

recipient_phone.help: Recipient phone number in E.164 format (e.g. +14155551234). Used by every method.

phone_number_id.help: Meta Cloud API only. The numeric Phone Number ID from the Meta Business Manager (WhatsApp > Phone Numbers). Used to build /v21.0/<phone_number_id>/messages.

access_token.help: Meta Cloud API only. Permanent system-user access token from the Meta Business Manager. Stored encrypted at rest.

gateway_url.help: Self-hosted gateway only. Base URL of your own WhatsApp gateway (Baileys, wa-gateway, etc.). The plugin POSTs {title, message, phone} to <gateway_url>/send.

gateway_token.help: Self-hosted gateway only. Bearer / API-key token presented as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Stored encrypted at rest.

business_api_url.help: Business Bot Platform only. Full endpoint of the platform's send-message route (e.g. https://waba.360dialog.com/v1/messages or your Twilio WhatsApp API base).

api_key.help: Business Bot Platform only. Platform API key sent in the D360-API-KEY header (or X-API-Key, depending on the platform). Stored encrypted at rest.

provider_url.help: Third-party SaaS only. Base URL of the provider's send-message endpoint. The plugin POSTs {to, from, body} to <provider_url>/messages.

provider_api_key.help: Third-party SaaS only. Provider API key (or Account SID + Auth Token for Twilio). Stored encrypted at rest.

provider_from.help: Third-party SaaS only. Sender identifier expected by the provider (Twilio WhatsApp 'From' number, MessageBird originator, Gupshup app id, etc.).

page.title: WhatsApps
page.subtitle: Route workflow, alert, and backup events to a WhatsApp phone number via one of four connection methods: Meta Cloud API, self-hosted gateway, WhatsApp Business API platform, or a third-party SaaS provider. The plugin handles Test (cheap credential round-trip) and Send (real message to the recipient) — there is no OAuth flow because WhatsApp providers use long-lived tokens.
page.registerHint: Add a channel from the host's Notifications > Channels page and pick "WhatsApp" as the channel_type.

form.channelBody: Pick the connection surface that matches how your WhatsApp account is set up. Cloud API is the official Meta route. Gateway is for self-hosted Baileys / wa-gateway deployments. Bot covers 360dialog-style platforms. SaaS covers Twilio, MessageBird, Gupshup, and similar providers.
form.differCloud: **Cloud API** — posts to `https://graph.facebook.com/v21.0/<phone_number_id>/messages` with a `Bearer` token. Use the Meta Business Manager’s permanent system-user token.
form.differGateway: **Self-hosted Gateway** — posts `{ phone, title, message }` to `<gateway_url>/send`. Your gateway is responsible for talking to the WhatsApp Web / multi-device API underneath.
form.differBot: **Business Bot Platform** — posts a Cloud-API-shaped body to `<business_api_url>` with the `D360-API-KEY` header. 360dialog and similar providers expose a Cloud-API-compatible surface.
form.differSaas: **Third-party SaaS** — posts `{ to, from, body }` to `<provider_url>/messages`. Twilio operators should set the API key to `<SID>:<AuthToken>` — the plugin switches to HTTP Basic auth automatically.

step1.body: Pick a connection method on the left. Cloud API = official Meta route (permanent system-user token). Gateway = your own Baileys/wa-gateway server. Bot = a WhatsApp Business API platform (360dialog etc.). SaaS = Twilio, MessageBird, Gupshup, or similar provider.

step2.body: Enter the recipient phone number in E.164 format (e.g. +14155551234). Every method uses this field — there is no per-method recipient override.

step3.body: Cloud API only: in the Meta Business Manager, open WhatsApp > Phone Numbers and copy the numeric Phone Number ID. The plugin POSTs to /v21.0//messages.

step4.body: Cloud API only: create a permanent system-user access token in Business Settings > System Users with whatsapp_business_management + whatsapp_business_messaging permissions. Paste it into the Access Token field. The token never expires; rotate by issuing a new one in the Business Manager.

step5.body: Cloud API only: register your sender phone with at least one message template in the Meta Business Manager. WhatsApp blocks the first 24 hours of conversations initiated by the business; templates bypass that window.

step6.body: Gateway only: deploy a Baileys / wa-gateway instance that exposes a JSON POST endpoint at /send accepting { phone, title, message } and an /test endpoint returning 2xx for valid bearer tokens. The plugin uses Bearer auth against /send.

step7.body: Gateway only: configure the gateway with your WhatsApp multi-device session (scan the QR code with the WhatsApp app). The gateway is responsible for keeping the session alive.

step8.body: Bot only: pick a platform that exposes a Cloud-API-compatible send endpoint (360dialog is the most common). Create an account, set up a WhatsApp Business sender, and copy the API endpoint URL into Business API URL.

step9.body: Bot only: copy the platform's API key into the API Key field. The plugin sends it as D360-API-KEY (360dialog convention) plus Authorization: Bearer as a fallback for OAuth-style platforms.

step10.body: SaaS only: create an account with your provider (Twilio, MessageBird, Gupshup, Plivo, …) and provision a WhatsApp-enabled sender. Copy the sender identifier (Twilio: "whatsapp:+14155550000", MessageBird: originator, Gupshup: app id) into the Provider From field.

step11.body: SaaS only: copy the provider's API key into the Provider API Key field. For Twilio, set it to ":" — the plugin detects the colon and switches from Bearer to HTTP Basic auth automatically.

step12.body: Paste the credentials for your chosen method into the matching fields. Click Save, then click Test connection. Test issues a cheap credential round-trip (GET for Cloud API, POST /test for gateway, GET /contacts for bot, dry-run POST for SaaS) — it never delivers a real message to the recipient phone.

step13.body: Once the channel is saved, route workflow or alert events to it from Settings > Notifications > Rules. Delivery is fire-and-forget: a failed Send is logged in the audit log and surfaced in the host toast, but the host does not retry.
